messages:
ashley: heads up — noticed a 25–35% CPU increase on host-preproc during peak RPS. flame shows a lot of time in host parse/tokenize + KV cache hot-shard contention. attaching quick profile snippet below.

mike: can you paste the flame lines? also which region and image?

ashley: us-west-2, image: host-preproc:v3.2.1-canary

ashley: flame excerpt (top stacks):
```
HostPreproc.parse_stream 45.2%  // parsing + tokenization loops
KVCache.lock_wait         18.7%  // hot-shard contention
HTTP2.writev              12.4%  // many small frames
TokenizePool.alloc         8.9%  // allocs on each req
Other (syscalls)           4.8%
```

ravi: that KV number explains the CPU ripple. looks like one shard is getting hammered by short chat requests — leads to constant eviction/lock churn and then parsing can't batch.

lina: also seeing increased HTTP2 frame counts in the traces. small streaming chunks -> lots of writev syscalls. gRPC messages per request jump from ~6 -> ~84 for the affected traces.

mike: do we have per-request token counts? are these single-turn short prompts?

ashley: most are 8–40 tokens user prompts with streaming enabled. KV hits are high but the hot keys are the same few convs.

ravi: quick mitigation plan: 1) enable shard-level backoff (stub) to spread writes across adjacent shard when hot detection triggers 2) pool tokenizers to avoid per-request allocs 3) coalesce small streaming chunks on host egress 4) tune batching window for small-token requests so they can join even with short latency budget.

lina: +1 for coalescing — we have a flag ingress.coalesce_chunks that was disabled last quarter. can we canary it on the canary fleet? it should reduce writev count dramatically.

ashley: ran a micro-benchmark locally with coalesce_chunks=true and tokenizer pool size 16:
```
benchmark: 1k concurrent short requests (avg 18 tokens)
baseline (no coalesce, pool=2): p95 latency 420ms, host CPU 78%
coalesce + pool=16: p95 latency 320ms, host CPU 52%, grpc_frames/request 9
```

mike: nice. what about KV changes? shipping shard-level backoff is more invasive. any quick config flips?

ravi: short-term: increase KV cache shard_count from 64 -> 256 for the canary group (reduces hot probability) and enable per-key soft-ttl to reduce eviction churn. that should buy us time to roll a proper backoff.

ashley: I've queued a canary: host-preproc:v3.2.1-canary+coalesce with shard_count=256 and tokenizer_pool=16. ingress-bot: start canary deploy for group "canary/host-preproc-4"

ingress-bot: Deploy queued: canary/host-preproc-4 -> host-preproc:v3.2.1-canary+coalesce (rolling 5 hosts). ETA 6m.

lina: monitoring hooks to watch:
- host.cpu (per-host)
- kv.lock_wait (per-shard)
- grpc.frames_per_request
- host.parse_p95
add alert if host.cpu > 65% or grpc.frames/request > 20 or kv.lock_wait spikes 10x.

mike: also update batching heuristic: window_ms for short requests -> 6ms (was 2ms), min_batch_tokens=8. should let a few tiny requests coalesce without hurting latency.

ravi: note: kernel selection hints — we can add a 'low-latency' hint from ingress for short-token streams so runtime picks the inference kernel tuned for small sequences (reduces HW kernel overhead and keeps GPU latency stable). filing a follow-up RFC.

ashley: can someone grab a flame after canary is up and paste stack comparison? want to verify KV lock_wait drops and writev syscalls reduce.

lina: I'll watch dashboards and post results. initial canary started. ping me if you need logs from host 10.12.4.22.

mike: if this buys us time we can roll to prod and then schedule a medium-term change for shard-level backoff + smarter key placement.

ashley: thanks — I'll follow up with data. (feel free to ping me in thread). :thumbsup:

lina: update 10m later: canary p95 dropped from 420ms -> 312ms, host CPU down ~26%, kv.lock_wait median halved, grpc.frames/request median 8. looks promising.

ravi: sweet. I'll draft the RFC for backoff + kernel-hint API.

mike: nice job. we'll keep canary for 2h then promote if stable.

ashley: leaving notes in the ticket with config diffs and benchmark logs.

lina: adding a quick grepable log snippet for detection rule if anyone wants to run locally:
```
grep -E "KVCache.lock_wait|HTTP2.writev|TokenizePool.alloc" host-preproc.log | tail -n 200
```

ashley: closing loop later with flame diffs. thanks team.
